items.title: feat(services): IEmbeddingService — batched in-process embeddings via Arctic Embed (ONNX)

labels.name: performance
labels.description: Memory, CPU, latency, or resource usage

items.body:
### Use case

The framework has no embedding primitive. Servers wanting semantic dispatch, RAG over tool outputs, dedup of result rows, or "find related" surfaces each add their own deps and re-solve the same compute problem: model lifecycle, cache location, warm-up, and batching.

| Surface | Need |
|:---|:---|
| Tool dispatch | Pre-rank tool definitions by query similarity so agents pick the right tool faster |
| Resource lookup | Semantic search across a resource catalog without rolling a separate index |
| Server-owned vault / corpus indexing | Downstream consumers: cyanheads/obsidian-mcp-server#72 (semantic search over Obsidian vaults), and `cyanheads-mcp-server`, which hand-rolls the same runtime today |

### Proposed API

Ship an in-process embedding **compute** primitive backed by [Snowflake Arctic Embed](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-l-v2.0) (Apache 2.0) running via ONNX. No external service, no API keys, no rate limits — same shape as the existing canvas primitive: optional dependency, own subpath, loaded once per process.

**Storage is explicitly out of scope for this issue.** Compute and storage are separable concerns with different shapes: model + tokenizer + inference benefits from uniformity (one ONNX runtime, one model cache, one warm-up cost); vector storage lifetime and access pattern is server-shaped (ephemeral mid-call vs. persistent across restarts vs. replicated). The framework provides the vectors; callers own the store (#188).

```ts
// Accessor initialized in setup() from the service instance
const embedding = getEmbeddingService();

// Batched embed
const vectors = await embedding.embed(['doc body one', 'doc body two'], ctx, { mode: 'document' });
// → Float32Array[] — each vector is `outputDim` floats
//   (256 float32 values occupy 1024 bytes; packed int4 is a separate encoding)

// Single-text convenience
const queryVec = await embedding.embedOne('query text', ctx, { mode: 'query' });

// Metadata for callers that need to version their indexes
const info = embedding.info();
// → model/revision, outputDim, maxTokens, preprocessing policy, embeddingVersion
```

```dotenv
# Configuration — env-driven, following the CANVAS_* convention
EMBEDDING_MODEL=arctic-embed-m-v1.5   # default; or arctic-embed-l-v2.0
EMBEDDING_OUTPUT_DIM=256              # MRL truncation
EMBEDDING_MODEL_CACHE_DIR=            # default: HF_HOME, then TRANSFORMERS_CACHE, then <tmpdir>/<server>/hf-cache
```

### Alternatives considered

| Path | Verdict |
|:---|:---|
| OpenRouter `/v1/embeddings` | OpenRouter's embedding catalog has no Arctic models (verified via `/api/v1/embeddings/models`). Closest is `baai/bge-m3` — coincidentally the base of Arctic-l-v2.0. Worth a follow-up provider for users who want hosted, but doesn't satisfy "first-class semantic search without external service." |
| Ollama (`snowflake-arctic-embed2`) | Forces operators to run Ollama. Not viable for hosted Docker containers without bundling Ollama in the image. |
| HuggingFace Inference API | Adds HF token surface + new SDK. Network hop on every embed call defeats the latency win. |
| Cloudflare Workers AI | Arctic models appear deprecated in the 2026 catalog (Cloudflare now defaults to `@cf/google/embeddinggemma-300m`). Sidesteps Arctic entirely. |
| Bundle storage into this primitive (canvas+VSS as the canonical path) | Conflates compute and storage. Canvas is ephemeral per-tenant spillover by design (#97); persistent vault-adjacent indexing has a different lifetime and would have to work around the canvas. Storage stays caller-owned; a dedicated store primitive is in #188. |

In-process ONNX is the only path that gives operators a zero-config compute primitive while remaining swappable for hosted providers later behind the same `IEmbeddingService` interface.

### Additional context

Depends on: #527 — build as a `defineService` definition with `runtimes: ['node', 'bun']`.
Related: #188 (vector store), #208 (hosted providers), #532 (public exports and optional-service isolation). This primitive has its own contract and subpath rather than extending `ILlmProvider`.

### Storage — caller-owned

The framework does **not** prescribe a vector store for this primitive. Each caller picks what fits its lifetime and access pattern. Three reference recipes documented in the skill (not code in the framework surface):

| Recipe | Fits | How |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **In-memory** (`Float32Array[]` + linear cosine) | Tool-routing, small catalogs (<10K vectors), per-request lifetime | No deps. Caller holds the array; iterate + dot product. |
| **Canvas + DuckDB-VSS** | Mid-tool-call queries over result rows; tenant-scoped ephemeral | Caller registers a canvas table with a vector column; runs `INSTALL vss; LOAD vss;` (gated by #106's extension pattern); queries via `array_cosine_similarity()`. |
| **Server-owned persistent store** ([sqlite-vec](https://github.com/asg017/sqlite-vec), pgvector, [LanceDB](https://github.com/lancedb/lancedb)) | Persistent indexes outside any tool call — vault indexing, corpus search, replicated workloads | Caller persists the versioned embedding fingerprint alongside vectors and rebuilds incompatible indexes. |

`info().embeddingVersion` hashes a versioned, canonical descriptor: provider, immutable model/tokenizer revision, inference dtype, output dimension, pooling, query/document prefixes, truncation, and normalization. Model name and dimensions alone do not establish compatibility. Query and document modes must apply the model's different preprocessing rules, including renormalization after MRL truncation. [The model card](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-m-v1.5) documents query prompting and separate scalar compression.

Return float32 vectors initially. Model-weight quantization changes inference resources; packed int4 vector storage needs its own codec and distance contract and must not be represented as `Float32Array` or silently mixed into this API.

### Design / Tradeoffs

Philosophy: **ship the smallest viable default; expose the larger model for operators who need multilingual or long-context retrieval.**

| Model | Context | Languages | Default? |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `snowflake-arctic-embed-m-v1.5` | 512 tok | English | yes |
| `snowflake-arctic-embed-l-v2.0` | 8192 tok | Multilingual | opt-in |

Changing models requires re-embedding documents and queries even at identical dimensions. Measure artifact size, peak/resident memory, and cold/warm load time for the selected ONNX revision and dtype; model file size is not process RAM.

Why `m-v1.5` defaults:

1. **Image size.** The smaller model reduces the model artifact budget; measure the selected ONNX artifacts before documenting a size.
2. **Startup cost.** Services compose once per process, so model load is paid at startup; the larger model loads several times slower.
3. **The two clearest framework-side use cases** (tool-definition matching, short-text similarity) fit comfortably in 512 tokens. Long-doc and multilingual workloads justify the opt-in.

### Runtime choice

[`@huggingface/transformers`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers.js) (v4, formerly `@xenova/transformers`) — Bun-compatible, ONNX-backed, built-in tokenizer, model download into a configurable cache dir. Single dep, same pattern as DuckDB's lazy `@duckdb/node-api` import.

### Scope

- New `src/services/embedding/` with `IEmbeddingService` interface + `OnnxArcticProvider` implementation, exported from its own subpath
- `@huggingface/transformers` added as optional peer (lazy-imported, same as DuckDB)
- Eager model warm-up at startup. Reproduce the historical cold-cache/OTel conflict against the selected dependency versions before requiring instrumentation reordering; test cold and warm caches with telemetry enabled.
- Concurrent first callers share one load; a failed load clears so the next call retries
- Cache dir: `HF_HOME` / `TRANSFORMERS_CACHE`, else a writable tmpdir path, never `node_modules/.cache`
- Refused on Workers at init (#208)
- OTel spans on embed calls (`embedding.batch_size`, `embedding.model`, `embedding.duration_ms`, `embedding.tokens_in`)
- Skill: `framework-skills/api-embedding/SKILL.md` — public surface, storage recipes, Docker model-bake recipe
- Tests: smoke test for both model variants under `tests/smoke/embedding-onnx.test.ts`; load-once and retry-after-failure

### Out of scope

- **Storage and ANN search.** Framework provides compute; callers own persistence. A dedicated framework primitive is tracked in #188.
- **Hosted-provider embeddings** (OpenRouter, Cohere, Voyage). Tracked in #208 — `IEmbeddingService` should be the interface, with `OnnxArcticProvider` as one implementation and an `OpenAICompatibleProvider` as a future sibling that points at any OpenAI-shaped `/v1/embeddings` endpoint.
- **Multimodal embeddings** (image, audio). Arctic is text-only; future providers could extend the interface.
- **Reranker models.** Separate primitive; some Arctic variants ship rerankers but they have a different API shape.
- **Auto-chunking long inputs.** Caller's responsibility — framework refuses inputs over `info.maxTokens` and surfaces the limit.

items.title: [Firestore] Snapshot listeners stall under concurrent load after 26.0.2 "performance improvements"
items.body:
<!-- DO NOT DELETE
validate_template=true
template_path=.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug.md
-->

# Description

Cloud Firestore Android SDK 26.0.2 (BoM 34.4.0) introduced a severe performance regression where **snapshot listeners stall or deliver with extreme latency** under concurrent load. Downgrading to 26.0.0 (BoM 34.1.0) immediately resolves the issue.

The regression was introduced by the changes in 26.0.1–26.0.2 labeled as "performance improvements":

* #7376 — Replaced the deprecated AsyncTask thread pool with a self-managed thread pool
* #7370 — Internal memoization of calculated document data
* #7388 — Avoiding excessive Comparator instance creation
* #7389 — Using unsorted HashMap instead of sorted TreeMap

# Observed behavior

* First snapshot delivery per listener works normally (86–261ms)
* Subsequent snapshot deliveries stall for 5–60+ seconds or never arrive
* Dead silence periods where WatchStream is subscribed but no callbacks fire
* Cache loads that normally take 80–680ms degrade to 5+ seconds

# Expected behavior
Snapshot listeners should deliver consistently regardless of how many concurrent listeners are active, as they do on 26.0.0.

# Conditions that trigger the regression
These are all common, supported Firestore usage patterns:

1. 6–10 concurrent snapshot listeners (typical for tabbed UIs with dashboard widgets and detail editors)
1. Documents with 50+ fields, deeply nested maps, arrays of reference IDs, and small inline base64 strings (~3 KB)
1. Complex queries using Filter.or with multiple branches and whereIn filters
1. Background CPU work is optional — the issue reproduces without it, but concurrent CPU load (e.g. video encoding) makes it worse

# Reproduction
We've created a minimal Flutter reproduction app that uses an automated "canary writer" to measure snapshot delivery latency:

**Repository**: https://github.com/s2nventures/firestore-perf-rgn

## Steps:

1. Seed 30 large documents into a `perf_test` collection
1. Open 8 concurrent snapshot listeners with `Filter.or`, `whereIn`, equality, and nested field queries
1. Start the canary — writes to a canary document every 3 seconds and measures how long the snapshot takes to arrive (10s timeout = "missed")
