items.title: XPElevator Simulator — enhancement path (control + log)
items.body:
Control plane for the **canonical XPElevator**: the live virtual-customer training simulator on xpelevator.com (founder decision 2026-07-04 — the journeys build is dead; see #12, PAUSE'd, and the harvest into the-calling#21). Full audit evidence: comment below.

## What it is (audited live, 2026-07-04)
Next.js/OpenNext on Cloudflare Pages (`xpelevator.pages.dev`, account **outside LWT**; DNS zone IS in LWT). Trainees run simulated customer conversations in **three modalities** — chat (SSE), browser voice (Web Speech push-to-talk + hands-free), and **real phone calls via Telnyx** — against admin-authored scenarios (persona, hidden goal, difficulty), then get scored /10 against weighted per-role criteria. Admin: criteria, job titles, scenarios, job↔criteria links, **multi-tenant orgs** (FREE/ENTERPRISE plan field). Single-player only. NextAuth credentials; Groq direct for the LLM.

## 🔴 Live issues found (exist TODAY, independent of any plan)
1. **The scoring engine is DOWN**: the Groq API key is expired (`/api/debug/groq` → 401 expired_api_key). Every session score is null — the product's core loop has never produced a real score on this deploy.
2. **All `/api/*` reads are unauthenticated**, and `/api/scenarios` leaks the scenarios' **hidden hints** the admin UI promises employees can't see — defeats the product mechanic and breaks tenant isolation.
3. Demo-grade posture: test data only (2 empty orgs), no billing/pricing/signup surfaces (404), no Sentry/PostHog, no security headers, inconsistent data layer.

## 🔒 Phase 0 — Founder inputs (everything else is blocked on these)
- [x] **Where is the source?** ~~Not on GitHub (searched) and not in the LWT CF account.~~ RESOLVED (comment 2026-07-04): branch `copilot/review-codebase-security` in THIS repo, tip `1eb7977a`.
- [x] **Access to the CF account hosting `xpelevator.pages.dev`** — RESOLVED: no external account needed; redeploy fresh into LWT (CF_API_TOKEN/CF_ACCOUNT_ID staged).
- [x] **Groq account access** to rotate the expired key — RESOLVED: org GCP-SM `GROQ_API_KEY` is valid (staged as repo secret); org LLM-chain switch stays Phase 5.
- [x] Confirm monetization: **B2B seat-based subscription** (per active trainee/mo, tiered chat → +voice → +phone) on the shared Stripe platform account. — ANSWERED 2026-07-08 (founder-delegated, reconciled from Factory#1952). Foundation shipped: PR #36 (seat-plan catalog `src/lib/plans.ts` + public `GET /api/plans`, tiers chat → +voice → +phone).

## Phase 1 — Restore + migrate (needs source)
- [x] Restore scoring (valid LLM credential) — verify a session produces a non-null score with your own eyes
- [x] Migrate the Pages project into the LWT account: deploy to new project → verify on *.pages.dev → flip the (LWT-owned) CNAME. Zero-downtime. — DONE 2026-07-05: cutover executed + verified (PR #23/#25). apex + www repointed `CNAME → xpelevator-sim.pages.dev`; Pages custom-domain `active`; `xpelevator.com` build fingerprint `3002eded03df2412` == `xpelevator-sim.pages.dev` (run 28740972547). Old project left dark + untouched.
- [x] Secrets into the org GCP SM/WIF pattern (the expired-key incident is exactly what centralized rotation prevents) — **DONE 2026-08-18** (PRs #247, #250, #251, #252): every deploy-critical secret now sources from GCP SM validated SM-first with a GitHub-secret no-lockout fallback — CF creds (#247), `DATABASE_URL` deploy-Pages-secret (#250) + migrate-job (#251), `GROQ_API_KEY` (#250), and `AUTH_SECRET` via `XPELEVATOR_AUTH_SECRET` (#252). Verified with own eyes on Deploy run 32088224486 (`36fba7ac`): `CUTOVER RESULT: DATABASE_URL=PASS GROQ=PASS AUTH_SECRET=PASS` (all GCP SM) + production `/api/health` 200 (no lockout on the one-time AUTH_SECRET session rotation, founder-pre-cleared). Standing Law 3 (one source of truth) satisfied; the PR #31 monitor remains as the expired-credential alarm.
- [x] Uptime checks on /api/health + a scoring canary — DONE 2026-07-06 (PR #31): `.github/workflows/uptime-monitor.yml` — health probe every 15 min (`/api/health` 200 on xpelevator.com + the pages.dev alias, plus a direct Groq `/v1/models` credential probe that catches an expired key before scoring silently nulls) and an end-to-end scoring canary every 6h that drives a full authenticated session on the live branded domain and asserts a NON-NULL score, then prunes old canary sessions. Any failure opens/updates a single GitHub alert issue. Verified on the merge-triggered run 28765492983 (both jobs green): xpelevator.com/api/health→200 ok:true, Groq→200 LIVE, session dad64d13→7/7 non-null scores avg 6.86/10.

_Phase 1(a) prerequisite (revised strategy, comment 2026-07-04) — DONE 2026-07-05:_ journeys `main` preserved as `archive/journeys`; simulator branch promoted to the new `main` via PR #17 (squash-merged). `main` tree now equals the simulator branch (only deviation: `deploy.yml` auto-deploy disabled → `workflow_dispatch` only, pending the Phase 1(b) LWT deploy rebuild).

_Phase 1(b)+(c)+(d) (comment 2026-07-05) — DONE:_ new LWT Pages project `xpelevator-sim` deployed + verified (PR #21); live Neon DB `aged-butterfly-52244878` backed up + migrated to head (`add_org_user_model` baselined, `add_voice_type`+`add_fk_indexes` applied, status "up to date") and one full authenticated session verified a **NON-NULL score** on `xpelevator-sim.pages.dev` (PR #22, run 28736232109). Live-issue #1 (scoring DOWN) is fixed + verified end-to-end.

_Phase 1(e) — DNS cutover (comment 2026-07-05) — DONE:_ founder B2 pre-authorization satisfied (evidence posted), flip executed + verified — `xpelevator.com` + `www` now serve the LWT build `xpelevator-sim` (PR #23 flip, PR #25 verify; runs 28740476745 + 28740972547). Rollback snapshot captured in the flip run log.

## Phase 2 — Close the security holes (highest-priority correctness work)
- [x] Auth on every /api/* read; kill the hidden-hint leak (test: unauthenticated /api/scenarios must NOT return script.hints) — DONE 2026-07-05 (PR #26): live `xpelevator.com` /api/{scenarios,jobs,criteria} → **401** for anon callers, and the anon `/api/scenarios` body exposes no `hints`/`customerObjective`/`customerPersona`; sanitizer also applied to `/api/scenarios/[id]` + session payloads (`/api/chat`, `/api/simulations`). Verified runner-side, deploy run 28745544626.
- [x] Enforce orgId tenant isolation at the API layer (schema has it; API ignores it) — DONE 2026-07-05 (PR #28 + #29): the cross-tenant IDOR on `GET /api/chat?sessionId=` is closed. Verified on the live deploy (run 28755424092 step 13): anon read → **401**, cross-tenant (other-org user) read → **403** for both the JSON body and the phone-stream `?stream=true`, owner read → **200**. Shared `canAccessSession` (owner-or-same-org-admin) now used by chat GET/POST + scoring; 9 unit tests; race-free proof wired as a permanent post-deploy gate in `deploy.yml`. (Cross-org `/api/orgs/*` admin governance deferred to the Phase 4 operator hierarchy — needs a platform-super-admin vs tenant-admin split.)
- [x] Security headers (CSP/HSTS/nosniff/X-Frame) + data-layer consistency pass — **headers DONE 2026-07-06 (PR #30)**: CSP (`frame-ancestors 'none'`, `object-src 'none'`, `base-uri`/`form-action 'self'`, `connect-src 'self'`), HSTS (`max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains`), `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy`, and `Permissions-Policy` (keeps `microphone=(self)` for voice) on **every** worker response. Verified on live `xpelevator.com` + `xpelevator-sim.pages.dev`, document + `/api/health`, and wired as a permanent post-deploy gate (run 28759891246). CSP is nonce-less for now (permits `'unsafe-inline'`/`'unsafe-eval'` for scripts to avoid white-screening Next.js hydration) — nonce-hardening + the **data-layer consistency pass** deferred to Phase 3 (spine work).

## Phase 3 — Factory standards + spine rewrite
- [x] CI + quality gates + service-registry entry; Sentry + PostHog — DONE 2026-08-18 (PR #255, `472dc05`): `feature-registry.yml` added at repo root (Platform Standards Dimension 11; canonical `app: xpelevator`, schema-valid + resolver-reconciled to the existing app node), which was the last missing artifact on this line. Service-registry entry already present (Factory `docs/service-registry.yml` `id: xpelevator-sim`); Sentry #253 + PostHog #254 shipped; the deterministic §3-4 CI stack (quality/audit/unit/ui/coverage/build/smoke/migrations, aggregated by the required `ci` context) is complete.
- [x] **Rewrite this repo's design spine** (docs/VISION|ARCHITECTURE|REQUIREMENTS still describe the dead journeys product) around the simulator, per PLATFORM_STANDARDS §16 — DONE 2026-07-09 (PR #37, `336d30a`): three-file spine established — `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` rewritten to the §16 shape (`verified: 2026-07-09`, Current context/containers + Target + Gap + Key Decisions), new `docs/VISION.md` + `docs/REQUIREMENTS.md` (R-001…R-903), ADR-0001 (LWT redeploy), domain catalogs relocated to `docs/DOMAIN_REFERENCE.md`, stale/wrong API-reference dropped.
- [x] Repo cleanup per the what-dies list in the harvest review (the-calling#21 comment) — DONE 2026-08-18: the harvest "Dies with the product" deletion contract (`stripe.ts`, members routes/table, journeys DB catalog, milestone materialization, the 323-ln mock test suite) is verified **ABSENT file-by-file from `main` (`472dc05`)** via `git ls-tree`/`grep` — satisfied structurally by the Phase-1(a) branch swap (journeys → `archive/journeys`; Next/Prisma simulator promoted to `main`). No live code changed. Residue = the dead unmerged `plan/v1-world-class` branch (🔒 founder-gated deletion) + stale merged slice branches (separate hygiene slice). Evidence table in the slice comment.

## Phase 4 — Productize, CHANNEL-FIRST (founder directive 2026-07-05: we do NOT sell retail — operators do; we collect from the vending machine)
The buyer we build for = the OPERATOR (training consultancies, agencies, enablement/L&D shops) who owns end-client relationships. They buy wholesale, sell at their own retail, and the platform collects automatically. End-customer surfaces exist to make the operator look good, not to acquire retail.
- [x] Operator model on the existing multi-tenant scaffolding: self-serve operator onboarding → operator workspace, white-label branding (name/logo/colors), ability to create + manage client orgs beneath them (org.plan evolves into an operator→client hierarchy) — DONE 2026-08-18 (PRs #36, #257, #258): self-serve onboarding (`/api/orgs/[id]/clients` promotes STANDALONE → OPERATOR), operator workspace (`/operator`), white-label branding (R-049), and the full create + manage verb set — create / list / seat-tier allocate (#257) / rename + delete (#258, deploy run 32190206911, post-deploy gates green). Wholesale metering/invoicing is item 2 below (🔒 live-mode gate).
- [ ] Wholesale seat billing: operator buys seats at wholesale via Stripe (shared platform acct), sets own retail; automated metering + invoicing/rev-share (Stripe Connect) — zero-touch "vending machine" (test-mode first; 🔒 live-mode founder gate). _Foundation started 2026-07-08 (PR #36): seat-plan catalog + public `/api/plans`; tiers chat → +voice → +phone; Stripe binding by lookup_key, wholesale amounts remain a founder input._
- [x] Starter scenario-library packs — operators need sellable inventory on day one, per-vertical packs are their SKUs — DONE (verified live 2026-08-19; catalog PR #55, import R-047 / upgrade R-054 / status route): **6 per-vertical starter packs** — SaaS Support Essentials, Retail Frontline Care, Inbound Sales & Discovery, Sales & Motivational Coaching, Sales Floor Coaching, Personal-Development Coaching — each a role (job title) + 4 scenarios spread across difficulty (easy/medium/hard) and modality (chat/voice/phone). Public catalog `GET /api/scenario-packs` + operator `/library` surface are **hidden-mechanic-safe** (R-021: `getPublicPackCatalog()` strips every scenario `script` — persona/objective/hints — never leaked to prospects/trainees). Admin `import → org` materialises `job_titles` + `scenarios` rows (ADMIN-only, strict `orgId` scope, idempotent `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, `pack_version`-stamped), with opt-in `upgrade` (re-sync stale rows, never deletes) + `status` (per-pack import/upgrade state). Admin "Scenario Packs" UI wired (`/admin`). Verified live on `xpelevator.com` via Deploy run 32192130880 (`5871ae0b`, all 3 jobs success): post-deploy gates ✅ "scenario-library catalog + /library surface" (anon 200 both hosts + `"packs"` shape + no `customerPersona|customerObjective|hints|script` leak + `/library` copy-clean), ✅ pack import admin-gated (anon 401), ✅ pack upgrade admin-gated, ✅ pack status admin-gated.
- [x] Manager reporting + CSV/PDF export — the artifact operators show THEIR clients — **CSV DONE 2026-07-10 (PR #45, deploy #129):** admin-only, org-scoped `GET /api/reports/sessions` streams a completed-session CSV (per-session weighted score, `sum(score*weight)/sum(weight)`) with `Content-Disposition: attachment`; reuses `requireAuth(_, ADMIN)` (anon 401 / non-admin 403) + strict `orgId` filter (no cross-tenant leak); pure `src/lib/csv.ts` + `src/lib/report.ts` (Worker-safe, no `Buffer`), Download-CSV button on `/analytics`. Anon `GET /api/reports/sessions` → **401** verified on `xpelevator.com` + the pages.dev alias (run 29114213997 step 15), permanent post-deploy gate. **PDF export DONE** (not deferred — superseded; the spine row R-045 is `live`): `?format=pdf` returns the same tenant-scoped report via a hand-rolled Worker-safe renderer `src/lib/pdf.ts` (no `Buffer`/deps), covering own-org, per-client (R-063) and portfolio roll-up/summary (R-064/R-069). Unit `tests/unit/lib/pdf.test.ts` + `reports-sessions.test.ts`; permanent post-deploy gate probes anon `?format=pdf` + `scope=clients&view=summary&format=pdf` → 401 (`deploy.yml`). Shipped by `472dc05`, on `main` via Deploy run 363 (success).
- [x] Operator-facing demo/wholesale-pricing surface only — NO end-customer retail marketing site — DONE 2026-07-10 (PR #39, deploy #125): public `/pricing` renders the seat catalog channel-first (operator copy: "buy wholesale, set your own retail"; no hard-coded money, `currency: null`); reads `src/lib/plans.ts` (same source as `/api/plans`). Anon `GET /pricing` → **200** verified on `xpelevator.com` + the pages.dev alias (run 29059912101), all three tier names present, copy-clean (no "AI").
- [x] Copy pass: current UI says "AI-generated"/"the AI" throughout — rewrite to craft vocabulary (org rule: never "AI" in user-facing copy) — DONE 2026-07-10 (PR #41, deploy run 29082657876): every user-facing `AI` token purged to craft vocabulary (simulated customer / scoring engine / the simulator) across the admin panel, landing, and the chat SSE error message; zero `AI` tokens remain in any rendered surface. Deploy self-verify: `/api/health` 200 on `0ab89da3`; live landing fetch showed the new copy with no `AI`.

## Phase 5 — Differentiators

> Telephony note (founder 2026-07-05): a **Bandwidth** account is planned for serious voice work later; Telnyx is current. Keep the voice/telephony layer behind a provider abstraction so the swap is cheap — no deep Telnyx-specific coupling.

- [ ] LLM onto @latimer-woods-tech/llm chain (per-app CF AI Gateway first — ghost gateway 401s silently)
- [ ] Voice upgrade: Deepgram STT + ElevenLabs TTS (org telephony stack; Telnyx phone path already exists)
- [ ] Team/cohort analytics; adaptive difficulty; multiplayer role-play (parked until paying tenants exist)

## Kill-signals
No test→paid org within 60 days of billing live; median sessions/trainee <2 after week 1; managers don't trust the /10 scores; voice realism gap collapses the differentiator; CAC > ~12mo seat revenue.

## Standing rules
Loop disabled until Phase 0 unblocks. When re-armed: one verified slice per session, curl-with-your-own-eyes, spine maintenance per §16, 🔒 gates on Stripe live-mode/DNS flips/destructive actions.

_(Detailed sub-plans in comments: Phase E experience-overhaul (E0–E4) + the star-map extraction contract are unchanged and remain the authoritative breakdown for their scopes.)_

items.title: Epic: Memory & Recall

type.name: Epic
type.description: A large initiative composed of multiple features and stories.

items.body:
Agents that forget everything between conversations cannot act as co-workers. This epic gives the platform durable memory — and makes it something an administrator can reason about and a user can control, rather than a black box bolted to the side of a chat.

### What the platform remembers

Three kinds of memory, one mechanism. **User memory** holds distilled facts about the person an agent is helping — their context, their preferences, how they work — learned from conversation rather than filled into a profile. **Organization memory** holds curated facts that hold for everyone in a pool: policies, project details, team conventions, written deliberately rather than inferred. **Conversation history** is the verbatim record, indexed so past discussions can be found by meaning instead of by thread title.

### How agents reach it

Memory is scoped along two axes: whose memory it is, and which agent learned it. An agent can be configured to recall only what it learned about the current user, everything any agent learned about them, only the organizational knowledge it contributed itself, or the whole organizational pool. Writes always persist the full metadata — the user, the writing agent, the originating conversation, the kind of record and when it was made — so retrieval can be as narrow or as broad as the configuration asks, and no second store is ever needed to answer a different question.

### How it is stored

Memory, conversation history and ingested knowledge share one substrate: one vector store, one retrieval path, one metadata schema. What separates them is metadata, not a parallel implementation. Above that substrate the platform keeps deliberate abstractions — agents configure memory, not vector namespaces; users see their memories, not chunks in a document tree. Unified access patterns underneath, purpose-shaped surfaces on top.

Extraction is owned by the platform rather than rented from a third-party library, so quality, latency, per-agent model choice and data residency are ours to tune — and improvements to the platform's own storage and retrieval apply to memory automatically.

### What users control

A user can see everything the platform has learned about them, correct it when it is wrong, and delete it. Deletion is real: it propagates to every index. And a user can only ever reach their own memory, never another's, however an agent is configured.

### Deliberately out of scope

Relationship graphs, and the graph database behind them: semantic retrieval over a single substrate covers the recall the platform actually needs, and the traversal capability was never used. Memory is also not exposed as admin-configurable knowledge databases, and no tenant data partition is introduced — tenant isolation remains the platform's existing access-rule ceiling.

### Sequence

Substrate prerequisites and the decoupling from the current third-party library come first. Then the migration that carries the metadata contract and the retrieval scopes. Then the capabilities built on top: conversation-history indexing and recall, consolidation, and the memory surfaces.

items.title: [RFC] Pluggable DSA Memory-Planning Solver + PyPTO Adapter
items.body:
**Design RFC for review** — feedback especially welcome on the Open Questions (sync-cost fidelity vs ptoas `GraphSyncSolver`, per-pool decomposition, and coordination with ptoas #913).

cc @Hzfengsy @lyfne123

---

# RFC: Pluggable DSA Memory-Planning Solver + PyPTO Adapter

## Status

**Draft — request for comments.** Author: Toni Boehnlein. 2026-07-08. Scopes the
*design* and *interface*; module layout and pass-order wiring are a follow-up.

## Summary

PyPTO plans local memory in two passes — `MemoryReuse` (coloring → buffers share a
`base_` Ptr) and `AllocateMemoryAddr` (bump → one max-sized slot per base group, no
region reclaim). No principled Dynamic Storage Allocation (DSA) formulation splits
*which buffers share* from *where each goes* this way, and the split is why a freed
region cannot be subdivided (issue #1908).

**Proposal:** a standalone, reusable **DSA solver** behind a field-standard interface
(buffers with lifetimes + sizes → offsets) plus a thin **PyPTO adapter**. The adapter
carries an **optional, capability-negotiated cost overlay** for NPU structure the
standard formulation drops — chiefly that *reuse isn't free*: overlapping two
lifetime-disjoint buffers manufactures a cross-pipe synchronization a pure peak
objective doesn't cost (today handled only by one hard-coded rule, #1949).
Off-the-shelf solvers consume the core; PyPTO's own (local-search) solver consumes
the overlay.

The hook is the principled solver. **As a byproduct it dissolves #1908** —
buffer-granularity packing subdivides freed regions natively. The fix ships on the
**v1** path and does **not** depend on the overlay/local-search research (**v2**).

## Motivation

`MemoryReuse`'s capacity-gated packing (#1949, now in main) separates pipelined
double-buffers to avoid a serializing false-WAR (#1475) — one hard-coded sync-aware
reuse decision. Two gaps remain: **(1)** that
awareness is one special case, not a general cost the placer optimizes → E2
generalizes it; **(2)** coloring is split from offset assignment, so a producer's
freed 64 KB slot can't be subdivided into a consumer's two lifetime-disjoint 32 KB
buffers → L0A overflow (#1908) → buffer-granularity planning closes it.

The standard DSA problem (min peak, no concurrent overlap) is a *projection* that
drops this overlay — capturing it without contaminating the portable core is the
design's real content.

**Strategic context.** ptoas has its own planner, and PTOAS #913 rewrites it toward a
func-level first-fit-by-lifetime planner (same algorithm class). The org keeps both
(pypto L3 / ptoas L2, `memory_planner` switch #1934) and consolidates later —
**coordinate with the #913 owners**; a pypto-owned L3 planner's niche shifts if the org
picks ptoas. Pursue anyway: (a) the reusable/benchmarkable solver is independent of
which planner ships; (b) the overlay models L3 reuse→sync info ptoas can't see; (c)
the fragmentation needs fixing on L3 now.

## Background

Core DSA — buffers each `(size, lifetime, align)` → offsets, min peak (or fit a cap),
no overlap for lifetime-overlapping buffers — recurs across systems; they differ in the
solver *and* which extensions they model (so the core is common, not identical).

| System | Problem object | Solver |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MiniMalloc (ASPLOS'23) | CSV `id,lower,upper,size` → `offset` | exact DFS over canonical solutions + pruning |
| TelaMalloc (ASPLOS'22) | same | heuristic search + ILP/CP-SAT |
| XLA | `BufferInterval{size,start,end,colocations}` → `Chunk` | `GlobalDecreasingSizeBestFitHeap` (heuristic, not optimal) + `NoFragmentationStatsHeap` (loose lower bound) |
| TVM USMP | `BufferInfo{size,align,conflicts[],pool_candidates[]}` → `PoolAllocation` | `greedy_by_size` / `greedy_by_conflicts` / `hill_climb` (local search) |
| ptoas (incl. #913) | free-region outline / `bufferLifeVec` per (core,pipe) | first-fit + region split/coalesce |

MiniMalloc's public CSV is single-pool/single-interval (no colocations/pins/multi-pool);
XLA's best-fit *heap* is a heuristic. **Benchmark:** MiniMalloc `challenging/` — A–K (11 instances, 154–454
buffers, 1 MiB), curated so greedy/best-fit *fail* → it exercises only the core and is
adversarial to best-fit.

## Goals / Non-goals

**Goals:** an IR-free `DsaSolver` library (reads the MiniMalloc CSV subset); a thin
adapter (IR → `DsaProblem`, `DsaResult` → MemRef addresses); an optional overlay; fix
the fragmentation as a byproduct (v1); evaluate vs MiniMalloc-optimal + the XLA lower bound.
**Non-goals:** not replacing ptoas's planner (L2); not solving sync/event-id allocation
(only *estimating* its cost); no new IR node.

## Design

### Core vs. overlay; constraint vs. cost

```
core DSA (portable)                overlay (pypto-specific, optional)
buffers {intervals,size,align,     E1 multi-interval liveness  ← CONSTRAINT (changes feasibility)
pool}, colocations, separations,   E2 reuse → sync cost        ← COST (re-ranks feasible set)
pinned, pool_caps → offsets        E3 bank-conflict cost       ← COST
```

The overlay is **not homogeneous**: E2/E3 (costs) re-rank the feasible set, but E1
changes *what is feasible* — a hull-only solver can report infeasible on an instance
that *fits*, so "infeasible ⇒ genuine OOM" is only defined once E1 is supported.

### Interface

```cpp
struct Buffer { BufferId id; std::vector<Interval> intervals; uint64_t size, align; PoolId pool; };
                                     // intervals: E1 union; core solver uses the hull

struct ReusePenalty { BufferId a, b; uint64_t penalty; };   // reason: cross_pipe|cross_core|event_budget
struct BankGeometry  { PoolId pool; uint64_t bank_size; uint32_t num_banks; };
struct CostModel {                                          // sparse DATA, not opaque callbacks
  std::vector<ReusePenalty> reuse_penalties;                // only cross-pipe lifetime-disjoint pairs
  std::vector<BankGeometry> banks;
  struct { double sync, bank, peak_slack; } weights;
};

struct DsaProblem {
  std::vector<Buffer> buffers;
  std::vector<std::pair<BufferId,BufferId>> colocations;    // hard SAME offset (must-alias)
  std::vector<std::pair<BufferId,BufferId>> separations;    // hard KEEP-APART even if lifetime-disjoint
  std::vector<PinnedBuffer> pinned;                         // fixed offset + (interval | whole-program)
  std::map<PoolId,uint64_t> reserved_base, pool_caps;
  std::optional<CostModel> cost_model;                      // nullopt = core-only
};

enum class SolveStatus { kFeasible, kInfeasibleProven, kBestEffortNoFit, kTimeout, kUnsupported };
struct ObjectiveValue { uint64_t peak, sync, bank; std::map<PoolId,uint64_t> peak_by_pool;
                        std::optional<uint64_t> lower_bound; bool optimality_proven; };
struct DsaResult { SolveStatus status; std::optional<DsaSolution> solution;
                   ObjectiveValue objective; std::vector<std::string> diagnostics; };

struct SolverCapabilities { bool multi_interval, cost_model, colocations, separations, pinned, multi_pool; };
class DsaSolver { public:
  virtual SolverCapabilities capabilities() const = 0;
  virtual DsaResult solve(const DsaProblem&) = 0;           // never "just returns a solution"
};
```

### Objective — mode-split

- **Core / benchmark** (`cost_model == nullopt`): minimize peak subject to no-overlap.
- **Overlay** (`cost_model` set): peak is a **hard per-pool constraint** (`peak_by_pool ≤
  cap`); among fitting packings minimize `w_sync·Σsync + w_bank·Σbank`. Peak enters
  *only* as feasibility — below-cap peak on transient L0 scratch is dead space, so
  shaving it must never cost a barrier. `weights.peak_slack` is an optional weak
  regularizer for backends that value footprint (default 0).

### Overlay extensions

- **E1 (constraint) · multi-interval liveness.** Today `var_liveness` is a single
  `[def,last_use]` hull → v1 uses hulls (parity); multi-interval is a later refinement
  (ptoas has `bufferLifeVec`).
- **E2 (cost) · reuse → sync.** Same-pipe reuse ≈ free; cross-pipe costs an event-id
  (palette 8 intra / 16 cross-core) or a full barrier. `reuse_penalties` estimates what
  ptoas's `GraphSyncSolver` charges. **Caveat:** the hardware pipe isn't in PyPTO IR at
  pass 30/31 (only *core* AIC/AIV; the pipe is assigned in ptoas) → the adapter
  reconstructs it from op kind + memory space.
- **E3 (cost) · bank conflict** on `offset mod bank_size`, coupled to `align` (if
  commensurate, alignment fixes the residue — weights aren't independent).

Pipeline depth is **not** an overlay item — the adapter pre-expands a depth-N buffer
into N staggered clones + `separations`, reducing to the core.

### Reuse edges (formal)

Two buffers induce a reuse edge iff: same pool; address intervals intersect; live sets
disjoint; a hazard crosses the ordered boundary. Colocated pairs are excluded (a
must-alias overlaps deliberately). Sub-region packing: each later tenant induces its own
edge with the prior tenant. The solver maintains a **per-move adjacency delta**
(sweep/interval index) — `cost(placement)` is not recomputed from scratch.

### Pluggability & degradation (honest)

MiniMalloc / XLA-heap / TVM-USMP are **offline oracles** over CSV or **reimplementations**
behind our interface — not in-process plugins. Core solvers don't honor
`colocations`/`separations`/`pinned`/multi-pool natively → the adapter preprocesses
(merge colocated → super-buffer; carve pins/separations as keep-outs). `SolverCapabilities`
advertises each. A core-only path merges `intervals` to hulls, drops the overlay, and may
run a **bounded** iterative "solve → add separations → re-solve" (governed — adding
separations shrinks the feasible set and can loop back into the fragmentation). `solve()` returns a
`DsaResult`: `kInfeasibleProven` = real OOM; `kBestEffortNoFit` escalates, it does not
error.

### Adapter + pass order

| Field | Source |
| --- | --- |
| `Buffer{size,align,pool}` | each MemRef; `pool` = memory space |
| `intervals` (E1) | `MemoryReuse` `var_liveness` — single hull today |
| `colocations` | `MaterializeSemanticAliases` (pass 29) must-aliases |
| `separations` | 910B `load`+`tpop_from_aic` hazard, `forbid_output_alias`, pipeline clones |
| `pinned` / `reserved_base` | `reserve_buffer` / per-space `reserved_start` |
| `reuse_penalties`, `banks` | reconstructed pipe class + `PassContext::GetBackendHandler()` |

Write-back: offset → MemRef address; colocations → shared base. The WAR is realized by
**ptoas's address-interval sync** at L3 (confirmed: PyPTO's tile path emits no
`set_flag`/`wait_flag`) → disjoint sub-region tenants aren't serialized (a **v1
correctness gate**). The solver replaces `AllocateMemoryAddr`'s offset walk and subsumes
`MemoryReuse`'s opportunistic half; pass 29 must-aliases + the hazard guard stay inputs.

**v1 must include both** the buffer-granularity fragmentation fix **and** pipeline-clone
separation (the #1949 clones become `separations`, the capacity shed becomes separation
relaxation on overflow). Otherwise peak-only v1 collapses the clones and **serializes
pipelined kernels**, a regression invisible to a "peak ≤ bump" gate.

## Affected Files (coarse)

- `src/ir/transforms/dsa/` — **New** — IR-free library (types, best-fit-decreasing,
  exact DFS, local search, CSV subset I/O, independent validator).
- `src/ir/transforms/allocate_memory_addr_pass.cpp` — **Modify** — replace the bump with adapter + solver.
- `src/ir/transforms/memory_reuse_pass.cpp` — **Modify** — reduce to liveness + must-alias + separations + hazard guard.
- `include/pypto/ir/transforms/` (**New** adapter header); `tests/ut/ir/transforms/` (**New/Modify**).

## Testing Plan

- **Standalone:** A–K — exact DFS owns feasibility;
  report peak vs MiniMalloc-optimal (ground truth), and the loose `NoFragmentationStats`
  bound only where no optimum is known (don't report the NoFrag gap as achievable).
- **Independent validator** on every output (caps, align, pins, colocations, separations,
  no-overlap, objective recompute); **differential** small-instance tests vs the exact
  solver; **proven-infeasible** and **timeout** tests.
- **#1908 regression:** the A-stationary chained matmul now fits; retire the
  output-stationary workaround (`test_chained_matmul_uses_mat_scratch`).
- **No regression:** per-kernel peak ≤ bump **and** a pipeline-clones-stay-distinct assertion.
- **Overlay:** cheap (same-pipe) vs expensive (cross-pipe) collapse both fit → cost-aware
  solver picks cheap. **E1:** instance that fits only with multi-interval. Determinism +
  CSV round-trip.
- **Before v2 defaults:** a **model-vs-measured** study — `Σreuse_penalty` vs actual
  ptoas event-ids/barriers (a one-round ptoas feedback may beat a static heuristic).

## Security

Compile-time resource exhaustion only: exact solvers are offline/test-only; in-pass
solvers are time-boxed → `kTimeout` → deterministic fallback (best-fit / bump). No
secrets, no runtime I/O.

## Alternatives

- **A · group-granularity first-fit** (the issue's literal proposal): insufficient — the
  pre-grouped producer slot stays co-live with the double-buffer → 96 KB. The minimal fix
  is **buffer-granularity** first-fit-by-lifetime.
- **B · sub-region reuse in `MemoryReuse`:** a non-portable, shape-specific patch.
- **Extend the solver contract with sync:** breaks core-solver pluggability → optional
  overlay instead.
- **Two RFCs (fix vs. research):** rejected — the **v1-independent-of-v2** rollout gives
  the decoupling without splitting the document.

## Rollout

Level3-first; **v1 is independent of and can land ahead of v2.**
**v0** offline library + harness. **v1** the fragmentation fix + pipeline separation (flagged,
core only, gate = peak ≤ bump AND clones distinct; falls back to the bump). **v2** overlay
+ local search (gated on the model-vs-measured study and #913 coordination). Level2
untouched.

## Open Questions

- **Sync-cost fidelity (v2 crux):** is a pipe-pair + budget heuristic enough for
  `reuse_penalty`, or is a one-round ptoas feedback loop needed (re-couples the tools)?
- **Hard vs. soft** for scarce resources (event-ids, peak) — one general answer, not
  per-resource?
- **Pools genuinely fixed?** If a tile may live in L0A *or* Mat/L1, fixing `pool` at
  collection is the biggest modeling loss. If fixed (expected), the problem **decomposes
  into k independent per-pool solves** (E2/separations intra-pool) — state and exploit it.
- **Conditional non-conflict:** phi-family / branch-exclusive vars share despite
  overlapping hulls today; a pure interval-overlap solver drops this (raises peak on
  branch-heavy kernels). Encode as `colocations` + a `may_overlap` exemption list?

## References

Issues/PRs: #1908, #1949 (capacity-gated, merged), #1934 (planner switch); ptoas #913.
MiniMalloc (ASPLOS'23, `github.com/google/minimalloc`); TelaMalloc (ASPLOS'22); TVM USMP
RFC 0009; OpenXLA `heap_simulator`.

items.title: arch: consolidate on psycopg 3 (async) as the single Postgres driver, drop asyncpg
items.body:
### Context
`pyproject.toml` declares **two** Postgres drivers: `asyncpg` as the runtime driver and `psycopg[binary]` further down (see Evidence). Two drivers means two DBAPI behaviours to reason about — parameter styles, type adaptation, JSON codecs, pooling, error hierarchies — and the sync/async split it invites bites in tests (a sync psycopg connection and an async asyncpg connection cannot share a transaction, so a test that writes through one and reads through the other stops seeing its own data).

psycopg 3 is the PostgreSQL-community driver with first-class async (`AsyncConnection`, `psycopg_pool.AsyncConnectionPool`), pipeline mode, and a SQLAlchemy 2.x dialect (`postgresql+psycopg`) that serves **both** sync and async engines from one driver. Locking the template onto a single driver is an architectural principle we want every generated project to inherit.

### Change
- Switch every SQLAlchemy URL / DSN construction to `postgresql+psycopg://` (settings, alembic env, tests, docker-compose, copier-templated `.env` examples, docs).
- `create_async_engine(...)` on the psycopg dialect; keep pool settings equivalent (translate any asyncpg-only kwargs such as `server_settings`, `statement_cache_size`, `prepared_statement_cache_size`).
- Alembic async env uses the same dialect; `alembic upgrade head` and `downgrade base` verified against the test Postgres.
- Replace asyncpg-specific code paths (`asyncpg.exceptions.*`, custom JSON/UUID codec registration, `asyncpg.Connection` type hints) with psycopg equivalents (`psycopg.errors.*`, built-in JSON/UUID adaptation).
- Dependencies: drop `asyncpg`; make `psycopg[binary,pool]` the runtime dependency. Document in the Dockerfile that production images may prefer `psycopg[c]` built against libpq; keep `binary` as the default so generated projects work out of the box.
- Tests/fixtures: conftest engines and any raw-DBAPI helpers move to psycopg; keep the single-transaction-per-test pattern intact.
- Docs: ARCHITECTURE.md gains a "Single Postgres driver: psycopg 3" principle with the why above; CONFIGURATION-GUIDE / QUICKSTART DSN examples updated.

### Acceptance criteria
- `grep -ri asyncpg` across source, tests, docs, copier templates and `uv.lock` returns zero hits.
- All DB URLs use `postgresql+psycopg://`; no `postgresql+asyncpg` anywhere.
- `alembic upgrade head` then `alembic downgrade base` succeed against the test Postgres in CI.
- Unit and integration suites pass; coverage gate unchanged or higher.
- Generated-template validation matrix green.
- ARCHITECTURE.md documents the single-driver principle.
- CI green (pre-commit, unit, integration, coverage >= 90%, validate-template matrix); PR auto-merges on green.

### Evidence
- `pyproject.toml` runtime dep `asyncpg>=0.31.0` and a second driver `psycopg[binary]>=3.3.4` (pyproject.toml lines 11 and 177).
- Lesson recorded 2026-09-21 in the global wiki (`wiki/lessons/testing.md`): sync psycopg and async asyncpg connections cannot share a transaction in tests.

Depends on: #50
Part of the 2026-09 template upgrade sprint.

items.title: RFC: BLIS's declarative output: the Result document, and round-trip to input
items.body:
# RFC: BLIS's declarative output: the Result document, and round-trip to input

**Repo:** inference-sim/blis-schemas · **Status:** accepted; steps 1-4 delivered, 4a-7 open (see *Status* below) · **Epic:** inference-sim/inference-sim#1855 · **Sub-issues:** inference-sim/blis-schemas#4 (result type), inference-sim/inference-sim#1871 (emission), inference-sim/inference-sim#2054 (round-trip), inference-sim/inference-sim#2062, inference-sim/inference-sim#2070, inference-sim/inference-sim#2071 · **Origin:** [inference-sim/inference-sim discussion #1853](https://github.com/inference-sim/inference-sim/discussions/1853) (this RFC is its output half; its input half is inference-sim/inference-sim#1602) · **Builds on:** inference-sim/inference-sim#2021 (engine extraction), inference-sim/inference-sim#1901 (one simulator, two workload sources), inference-sim/inference-sim#1602 (one configuration document) · **Consumed by:** a sweep layer (`SweepSpec`, `SweepIndex` in blis-schemas `spec/sweep`).

State at the time of writing: blis-schemas `main` = [`6dfab32`](https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-schemas/tree/6dfab32a563e393658d3e82919db684633512b1d) (`v0.7.0`); inference-sim `main` = [`18135792`](https://github.com/inference-sim/inference-sim/tree/1813579275e3f782ecc1a83ef508017935121235) (pins blis-schemas `v0.7.0`, blis-latency-kernel `v0.3.0`, llm-d-router fork `v1.0.0-blis.1`).

## Status (2026-11-04)

Checked against blis-schemas `main` = [`a649e0f`](https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-schemas/tree/a649e0f) (`v0.10.0`) and inference-sim `main` = [`df31ab96`](https://github.com/inference-sim/inference-sim/tree/df31ab9696442a6d0ea70ad55bfed5f8e809618e) (pins blis-schemas `v0.10.0`, blis-latency-kernel `v0.5.0`, blis-vllm `v0.32.0-blis.1`, llm-d-router fork `v1.0.0-blis.2`). Sections *What exists today* and *Not in this RFC* below describe the state when the RFC was written.

**Delivered**
- `Clock: simulated` and the `Result` type, validator and example (inference-sim/blis-schemas#108, #4; PR inference-sim/blis-schemas#15), released in blis-schemas `v0.9.0`. Reference: `docs/reference/result.md`.
- `run` / `replay` emit the `Result` (JSON default, `--format yaml`, `--output`, `--view summary`); `--metrics-path` / `--results-path` deprecated; INV-6 and INV-13 restated over the `Result` (inference-sim/inference-sim#1871, PR inference-sim/inference-sim#2058).
- blis-config-search reads the `Result` (inference-sim/blis-config-search#20).
- The engine move this RFC builds on (inference-sim/inference-sim#2021, #2032, inference-sim/blis-schemas#102).

**Open**
- `--from-result`, `rerun_of` / `revision_changes`, round-trip tests: inference-sim/inference-sim#2054.
- Output-only flags that change the document without being recorded, and a field for closed-loop follow-ups: inference-sim/inference-sim#2062.
- `engine` section from `engine.Engine.Metrics`, series by reference: inference-sim/inference-sim#2070.
- Remove `--metrics-path` / `--results-path`: inference-sim/inference-sim#2071.
- The accuracy dashboard reads the `Result`: inference-sim/accuracy-dashboard#44.

**Where the shipped code differs from this text**
- **Window bounds.** The emitter states `first_arrival_after_warmup` / `last_completion` (derived), `profiling_start` / `profiling_end` (a replay's explicit window), and `simulation_start` / `simulation_end` (no measured completion), not `first_send_after_warmup`. `docs/examples/result.json` and `docs/reference/result.md` still show `first_send_after_warmup`.
- **Engine section.** Shipped shape: `engine.cluster` (step-interval series, cache hit rates, preemptions, KV figures, in-flight counts, `server_series`, `acceptance`, `whole_run`), `engine.instances`, and `engine.<pool role>.prefix_cache`. It is built by inference-sim from its own metrics, not from `engine.Engine.Metrics`, and `server_series` is inline, not referenced (Principles 5 and 6). Tracked in inference-sim/inference-sim#2070.
- **Whole-run values** are under `engine.cluster.whole_run`, not a second named window. `goodput.goodput_rps` is over the whole simulated run, not `window`.
- **Revisions.** `catalog` and `registry` carry a git `revision` (`-dirty` suffixed when the tree has uncommitted content), never a `release`. `engine.kind` is the literal `vllm` (inference-sim/inference-sim#2070).

**Open decisions**
- **JSON Schema.** [Discussion #1853](https://github.com/inference-sim/inference-sim/discussions/1853) proposed a JSON Schema generated from the Go types, published and checked in CI, so non-Go consumers can validate a `Result`. This RFC does not include one; today the contract is blis-schemas' Go `Validate`. To decide: publish one, or record the Go validator as the contract.
- **`convert`.** Whether `blis convert` emits a schema document describing the trace it produced, or stays trace-shaped: inference-sim/inference-sim#1875.

## Summary

BLIS's input is already declarative: a blis-schemas `Scenario` + `Deployment` names the model, hardware and serving configuration; the embedded llm-d router reads its own `EndpointPickerConfig`; the engine reads its own `engine:` block. Its output is not. A run prints a banner, a JSON object and plain-text sections to stdout, and writes a different JSON object to `--metrics-path`. Downstream tools parse that file by key name and must know which keys mean what.

This RFC adds the missing half and closes the loop between the two:

1. **A `Result` document** (`kind: Result`) in blis-schemas: what one BLIS run predicts (one configuration, one load, one seed), stated in the same metric vocabulary blis-schemas already uses for what a real run measured (`measurement.MeasuredRun`), so a prediction and a measurement compare by name and definition, not by convention.
2. **A complete input record.** The `Result` embeds everything the run was given, including the run-level controls (load, request count, seed, horizon, warmup, workload) that today exist only as CLI flags.
3. **Round-trip.** Feeding a `Result`'s embedded input back to BLIS reproduces the `Result` byte-for-byte outside one quarantined block, and a re-run on a newer BLIS is allowed and records what changed.

## What exists today

### Input (declarative, shipped)

| Piece | Where | Owned by |
|---|---|---|
| `Scenario` (model, cluster inventory, coefficients, `engine_version`, workload binding, acceptance and routing pins) | [`spec/scenario/scenario.go`](https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-schemas/blob/6dfab32a563e393658d3e82919db684633512b1d/spec/scenario/scenario.go) | blis-schemas |
| `Deployment` (pools: role, nodes, parallelism, `engine:`, labels; `offload`; `pd_transfer`; `router:`) | [`spec/deployment/deployment.go`](https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-schemas/blob/6dfab32a563e393658d3e82919db684633512b1d/spec/deployment/deployment.go) | blis-schemas |
| Router inputs: `router: {epp_flags, endpoint_picker_config, manifests}`, passed to the embedded llm-d router unopened | [`deployment.go#L49-L61`](https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-schemas/blob/6dfab32a563e393658d3e82919db684633512b1d/spec/deployment/deployment.go#L49-L61), [`embed/embed.go#L144`](https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-schemas/blob/6dfab32a563e393658d3e82919db684633512b1d/embed/embed.go#L144) | llm-d router (the schema references its files, never restates them) |
| Engine inputs: `engine:` block; moving to an engine-neutral envelope `{kind, upstream_version, config}` read only by the engine | [inference-sim/blis-schemas#102](https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-schemas/pull/102) (`engine/spec.go`), [inference-sim/inference-sim#2032](https://github.com/inference-sim/inference-sim/issues/2032) | blis-vllm (#2021) |
| Run-level inputs: `--rate` XOR `--concurrency`, `--num-requests`, `--seed`, `--horizon`, `--workload` / `--workload-spec`, trace files | CLI flags only ([`cmd/root.go#L853-L854`](https://github.com/inference-sim/inference-sim/blob/1813579275e3f782ecc1a83ef508017935121235/cmd/root.go#L853-L854), [`#L2151-L2155`](https://github.com/inference-sim/inference-sim/blob/1813579275e3f782ecc1a83ef508017935121235/cmd/root.go#L2151-L2155)) | **no document** |

### Output (not declarative)

- **stdout:** `=== Simulation Metrics ===`, a `MetricsOutput` JSON object ([`sim/metrics.go#L507`](https://github.com/inference-sim/inference-sim/blob/1813579275e3f782ecc1a83ef508017935121235/sim/metrics.go#L507)), then plain-text sections: fitness, anomaly counters, KV cache, per-SLO, per-model, per-tenant, sessions, P/D, trace summary ([`cmd/root.go#L1879-L1956`](https://github.com/inference-sim/inference-sim/blob/1813579275e3f782ecc1a83ef508017935121235/cmd/root.go#L1879-L1956); the same in `cmd/replay.go`).
- **`--metrics-path`:** the same struct ([`sim/metrics_utils.go#L94`](https://github.com/inference-sim/inference-sim/blob/1813579275e3f782ecc1a83ef508017935121235/sim/metrics_utils.go#L94)) plus fields that are file-only so that stdout stays byte-identical across hosts and catalog checkouts: `cache_hit_rate`, `catalog`, `overrides`, `pd`, `server_series`, the measured-window metrics (`request_itl_*`, `step_interval_*`, `output_throughput_tok_s`, ...), `whole_run`, `kernel_provenance`, build versions, `acceptance`, `prefix_cache`, per-request rows.
- **`replay --results-path`:** a third shape, `[]SimResult` per-request rows for `calibrate` ([`sim/workload/calibrate.go#L347`](https://github.com/inference-sim/inference-sim/blob/1813579275e3f782ecc1a83ef508017935121235/sim/workload/calibrate.go#L347)); `calibrate` is being removed (#1901).
- **Metric meaning is carried by key names and comments.** `itl_mean_ms` is the per-decode-step interval; `request_itl_mean_ms` is the per-token interval that benchmark harnesses report as TPOT. Under speculative decoding the two differ by the acceptance length. Consumers must know this to read the file correctly.
- **Consumers:** the accuracy dashboard reads `ttft_mean_ms` and `request_itl_mean_ms` from `--metrics-path`; config search reads `tokens_per_sec`, `itl_p99_ms`, `ttft_p99_ms`, `injected_requests`, `completed_requests`; neither has a schema to validate against.

### The measured side (declarative, shipped)

`measurement.MeasuredRun` ([`spec/measurement/measurement.go#L25`](https://github.com/inference-sim/blis-schemas/blob/6dfab32a563e393658d3e82919db684633512b1d/spec/measurement/measurement.go#L25)) describes a real serving run: the configuration that ran (`model`, `cluster`, `deployment`, `router`, `workload`), the client (`harness`, `seed`, `num_prompts`, `burstiness`, warmups, duration), `metric_defs` (each metric's `formula`, `statistic`, `population`, `clock`, start and stop events, `percentile_method`, `unit`), and `points` keyed by offered `load` (`concurrency` and/or `request_rate`). It is the document predictions are scored against.

## Principles

1. **One document out, one byte stream.** stdout is the `Result` document, JSON by default and YAML with `--format yaml`; `--output <file>` writes the same bytes. Human-readable views are renderings of the document, never a second emission.
2. **Same vocabulary for predicted and measured.** A `Result` metric is named and defined with the `measurement` vocabulary (`Formula`, `Statistic`, `Population`, `Clock`, `MetricUnit`). Scoring a prediction is a join on metric name and load, with the definitions checked equal.
3. **Self-describing and replayable.** A `Result` embeds the fully resolved input (`Scenario`, `Deployment`, run controls, policy bundle) and the revisions of every input it read. That embedded input, given back to BLIS, reproduces the `Result`.
4. **Determinism has one exception, and it is a block.** Everything outside `runtime` is a deterministic function of the resolved input and the input revisions. `runtime` holds wall-clock time, host and build-environment facts, and nothing else.
5. **Owners report their own facts.** BLIS (inference-sim) owns time, request accounting and latency distributions. The engine reports its own series (`engine.Engine.Metrics`, #2021 B7); the embedded router reports its own requirements (`embed.Requirements`); the latency kernel reports coefficient provenance. The `Result` carries each in its own section and inference-sim does not reinterpret them.
6. **Bulk data stays external.** Per-request rows, time series and traces are referenced by path and `sha256`, never forced inline, the same rule `workload.TraceRef` already follows.
7. **Self-identify by `kind` + `schema_version`.** The `Result` carries `kind: Result` and a `schema_version` integer, as `MeasuredRun` does.

## Proposal

### A. The `Result` document (blis-schemas `spec/result`)

One `Result` per BLIS run: one configuration, one load, one seed. JSON is the default encoding; `--format yaml` emits the same document as YAML.

```json
{
  "kind": "Result",
  "schema_version": 1,
  "name": "qwen3-32b-h100-pd@c64-s1",

  "input": {
    "scenario":   { "...": "Scenario as resolved (catalog names kept, defaults filled)" },
    "deployment": { "...": "Deployment as resolved, incl. router: and the engine block" },
    "policy":     { "...": "the --policy-config bundle, verbatim, when one was given" },
    "run": {
      "load": { "concurrency": 64 },
      "num_requests": 2000,
      "seed": 1,
      "horizon_s": null,
      "warmup": { "requests": 128 },
      "workload": { "shape": "chatbot" }
    }
  },

  "revisions": {
    "blis": "v0.13.0",
    "blis_schemas": "v0.7.0",
    "blis_latency_kernel": "v0.3.0",
    "llm_d_router": "v1.0.0-blis.1",
    "engine": { "kind": "vllm", "upstream_version": "0.32.0", "release": "v0.32.0-blis.1" },
    "catalog": { "release": "0.3.0", "revision": "ba542f0" },
    "registry": { "release": "v0.2.0", "revision": "7f6662d" }
  },

  "rerun_of": null,
  "revision_changes": [],

  "metric_defs": {
    "output_tok_s":         { "formula": "output_throughput", "denominator": "profiling_window", "unit": "tokens_per_s" },
    "output_tok_s_per_gpu": { "formula": "output_throughput", "denominator": "per_gpu", "unit": "tokens_per_s" },
    "interactivity_mean":   { "formula": "user_tps", "statistic": "mean", "population": "per_request", "clock": "simulated", "unit": "tokens_per_s" },
    "interactivity_p50":    { "formula": "interactivity", "statistic": "p50", "population": "per_request", "percentile_method": "numpy_linear", "clock": "simulated", "unit": "tokens_per_s" },
    "interactivity_p90":    { "formula": "interactivity", "statistic": "p90", "population": "per_request", "percentile_method": "numpy_linear", "clock": "simulated", "unit": "tokens_per_s" },
    "ttft_mean_ms":         { "formula": "ttft", "statistic": "mean", "population": "per_request", "clock": "simulated", "unit": "ms" },
    "ttft_p99_ms":          { "formula": "ttft", "statistic": "p99", "population": "per_request", "percentile_method": "numpy_linear", "clock": "simulated", "unit": "ms" },
    "itl_p99_ms":           { "formula": "tpot_excl_first", "statistic": "p99", "population": "per_request", "percentile_method": "numpy_linear", "clock": "simulated", "unit": "ms" },
    "e2e_mean_ms":          { "formula": "e2el", "statistic": "mean", "population": "per_request", "clock": "simulated", "unit": "ms" },
    "request_throughput":   { "formula": "request_throughput", "denominator": "profiling_window", "unit": "requests_per_s" }
  },

  "window": { "start": "first_send_after_warmup", "stop": "last_completion", "duration_s": 312.4, "requests": 1870 },

  "metrics": {
    "output_tok_s": 10240.3,
    "output_tok_s_per_gpu": 640.0,
    "interactivity_mean": 41.7,
    "interactivity_p50": 43.3,
    "interactivity_p90": 35.1,
    "ttft_mean_ms": 182.0,
    "ttft_p99_ms": 431.5,
    "itl_p99_ms": 28.5,
    "e2e_mean_ms": 2904.7,
    "request_throughput": 6.0
  },

  "requests": {
    "generated": 2000,
    "rejected": 2,
    "injected": 1998,
    "completed": 1988,
    "still_queued": 0,
    "still_running": 8,
    "dropped_unservable": 0,
    "timed_out": 0,
    "routing_rejections": 0,
    "gateway_queue_depth": 2,
    "gateway_queue_rejected": 0,
    "gateway_evicted": 0,
    "gateway_expired": 0,
    "encode_routing_rejections": 0,
    "length_capped": 0
  },

  "goodput": {
    "targets": { "interactive": { "ttft_ms": 500, "itl_ms": 50 } },
    "goodput_rps": 5.7,
    "slo_attainment": 0.95,
    "per_class": { "interactive": { "completed": 1988, "met": 1889 } }
  },

  "breakdowns": {
    "pd": { "prefill_ttft_mean_ms": 90.1, "decode_ttft_mean_ms": 91.9, "kv_transfer_mean_ms": 7.2 },
    "per_model": {}, "per_tenant": {}, "per_adapter": {}, "sessions": {}
  },

  "engine": {
    "prefill": {
      "series": { "ref": "c64-s1.engine-prefill.jsonl", "sha256": "...", "interval_s": 1.0 },
      "final": { "vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc": 0.31, "vllm:num_preemptions_total": 0 },
      "resolved": { "...": "what the engine resolved from its config, e.g. acceptance supplied" }
    },
    "decode": {}
  },

  "router": { "requirements": { "disaggregates": true }, "rejections": { "by_kind": {} } },
  "kernel": { "prefill": { "evidenced": 41, "total": 44, "assumptions": [] }, "decode": {} },
  "saturation": null,

  "overrides": [ { "setting": "scheduler", "input": "fcfs", "run": "priority", "source": "--scheduler" } ],

  "artifacts": {
    "per_request": { "ref": "c64-s1.requests.csv", "sha256": "...", "rows": 1998 },
    "trace": { "header": "c64-s1.trace.yaml", "data": "c64-s1.trace.csv", "sha256": "..." }
  },

  "runtime": { "wall_clock_s": 18.4, "host": { "os": "linux", "arch": "amd64", "cpus": 24 }, "started_utc": "2026-10-27T15:02:11Z" }
}
```

Rules:

- **`input`** is the resolved input, not the command line: `scenario`, `deployment`, `run` (section B), and, when given, the `--policy-config` bundle as `policy`. A flag that overrode the scenario appears as the resolved value in `input` and as a row in `overrides`.
- **`metric_defs` + `metrics`** use `measurement.MetricDef` unchanged; a name means only what its definition says. One addition to the `measurement` vocabulary is needed: `Clock: simulated` (BLIS's events are on one simulated clock, with no client/server distinction; stating it keeps the comparison explicit). Percentile statistics (`p50`, `p90`, `p99`, ...) are already accepted by pattern, and BLIS's percentile (`CalculatePercentile`, rank `p/100*(n-1)`, linear interpolation) is the existing `numpy_linear` method. A metric BLIS computes that has no `measurement.Formula` is named in `engine` or `breakdowns`, not in `metrics`.
- **Standard metric names.** A `Result` and a `MeasuredRun` use the same names for the same definitions, so a report, a goal or a scorer reads either kind with no translation:

  | Name | Definition |
  |---|---|
  | `output_tok_s` | output tokens over the measured window |
  | `output_tok_s_per_gpu` | `output_tok_s` divided by the GPUs the deployment's pools use |
  | `interactivity_mean` | mean over requests of (output tokens − 1) / (E2E − TTFT), tokens/s/user |
  | `interactivity_p50`, `interactivity_p90` | 1000 / the p50 and p90 of per-request ITL, tokens/s/user |
  | `ttft_mean_ms`, `ttft_p50_ms`, `ttft_p90_ms`, `ttft_p99_ms` | time to first token |
  | `itl_mean_ms`, `itl_p50_ms`, `itl_p90_ms`, `itl_p99_ms` | per-request ITL per **token**, (E2E − TTFT) / (output tokens − 1) |
  | `e2e_mean_ms`, `e2e_p50_ms`, `e2e_p90_ms`, `e2e_p99_ms` | request latency |
  | `request_throughput` | completed requests over the measured window |

  `itl_*` is always per token. Today's `--metrics-path` `itl_*` keys are the per-decode-step interval, which under speculative decoding is the accepted length times the per-token value; in the `Result` that series is `engine`-reported as `step_interval_*`, never `itl_*`. A metric outside this table gets a name of the same form (`<quantity>_<statistic>_<unit>`) and its own `metric_defs` entry.
- **`window`** states the measured window. Today's file carries both whole-run and measured-window values of the same keys (`whole_run`); in the `Result`, `metrics` is always over `window`, and whole-run values, when wanted, are a second named window.
- **`requests`** is the conservation ledger, with every INV-1 term under its INV-1 name, including the six cluster-only terms that today's output does not serialize (so no CLI-level test can check the eleven-term form, #1746). The validator checks both clauses: `injected` equals the sum of the terminal buckets, and `generated` equals `injected + rejected`.
- **`engine`, `router`, `kernel`** are owned by those components. For vLLM, `engine.final` and `engine.series` carry `vllm:*` series by their vLLM names, the same series the embedded router scrapes. Today's `server_series`, `cache_hit_rate`, `prefix_cache`, `acceptance` and step-interval metrics move here.
- **`runtime`** is excluded from determinism and from the round-trip comparison. Nothing else is.
- **`rerun_of` + `revision_changes`** record lineage when a `Result` was produced from another `Result`'s input (section C): the source document's name and `sha256`, and every component whose revision differs, from and to. Both are empty on a fresh run.
- **Validation:** `Validate(Bundle{Result: r})` checks field shapes, that every `metrics` key has a `metric_defs` entry, the INV-1 sum, that `input.run.load` states exactly one of `concurrency` or `request_rate`, that `artifacts` references carry a `sha256`, and that `revision_changes` is empty when `rerun_of` is.

`evaluation.Run` is superseded for scoring by `measurement.MeasuredRun`; the `Result` does not extend either. A `Result` and a `MeasuredRun` compare point-by-point on `input.run.load` against `points[].load`, metric-by-metric on name, with `metric_defs` checked equal in every field except `clock` (`simulated` on the `Result`, `client` or `server` on the `MeasuredRun`).

### B. Run controls, and how sweeps use them

`input.run` holds what today exists only as CLI flags:

| Field | Flag today | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `load` | `--concurrency` XOR `--rate` | `measurement.Load`: exactly one of `concurrency`, `request_rate` |
| `num_requests` | `--num-requests` | int |
| `seed` | `--seed` | int |
| `horizon_s` | `--horizon` | optional |
| `warmup` | (workload spec) | optional; `requests` or `duration_s` |
| `workload` | `--workload`, `--workload-spec`, trace files | `workload.Binding`: catalog shape XOR trace reference |

- These stay flags on `run` and `replay`; the `Result` records the values the run used, so the input is complete. A standalone run-controls file is not part of this RFC.
- `load` reuses `measurement.Load`, so a `Result` lines up with `MeasuredRun.points[].load` without conversion.
- The scenario's own `workload` binding is the default; a flag that replaces it is recorded in `overrides`.
- **Sweeps** are defined outside BLIS, by `SweepSpec` (blis-schemas `spec/sweep`): a scenario, a baseline deployment, families of deployments over a grid of `Deployment` field paths, a concurrency ladder, seeds and goals. A sweeper expands it into resolved configurations and runs `blis run` once per configuration, ladder step and seed; each run writes one `Result`, and a `SweepIndex` lists them. BLIS reads no sweep document, and `SweepSpec.goals` name metrics from the standard table in section A.

### C. Round-trip: output → input → output

- **Contract:** `blis run --from-result R.json` reads `R.input` and the referenced artifacts (trace, catalog, registry at `R.revisions`). At the same revisions it produces a `Result` byte-identical to `R` outside `runtime`, `rerun_of` and `revision_changes`.
- **Determinism (replaces INV-6's stdout form):** the same resolved input at the same revisions yields a byte-identical `Result` outside `runtime`.
- **Run → replay (kept):** `run` with `artifacts.trace` set, then `replay` of that trace with the same `Scenario`, `Deployment` and `Run` (load from the trace), yields the same `metrics`, `requests` and `breakdowns`. This is the existing INV-13 test, stated over the `Result` document.
- **Re-running on a newer BLIS:** `--from-result` at a different BLIS, kernel, schema, router, engine, catalog or registry revision runs, and the new `Result` sets `rerun_of` to `R`'s name and `sha256` and lists every differing component under `revision_changes`:

  ```json
  "rerun_of": { "name": "qwen3-32b-h100-pd@c64-s1", "sha256": "..." },
  "revision_changes": [
    { "component": "blis", "from": "v0.13.0", "to": "v0.15.0" },
    { "component": "blis_latency_kernel", "from": "v0.3.0", "to": "v0.4.0" }
  ]
  ```

  An input field the newer BLIS no longer accepts is refused with the field named; a field it adds takes its default and is recorded in `overrides`. Comparing the two `Result`s' metrics is a diff of two documents; the new `Result` does not embed the old values.

### D. Emission (inference-sim)

- `run` and `replay` print the `Result` to stdout and nothing else, JSON by default; `--format yaml` selects YAML; `--output <file>` writes the same bytes as stdout.
- `--view summary` renders today's plain-text sections from the document to stderr, for humans.
- `--metrics-path` and `replay --results-path` keep their current content for one release, each file stating at its top that it is deprecated in favor of `--output`, then are removed.
- The engine's, router's and kernel's sections are filled from their own interfaces (`engine.Engine.Metrics`, `embed.Requirements`, `kernel.Kernel.Provenance`), so a new engine or router version changes those sections without an inference-sim change.

## Not in this RFC

- **Routing configuration.** It lives in the llm-d router's own files and reaches the simulator through `Deployment.router` and the `embed` contract; this RFC references it and adds nothing.
- **Engine configuration and the engine contract.** Owned by #2021 (inference-sim/blis-schemas#102, inference-sim/inference-sim#2032). The `Result.engine` section consumes `engine.Engine.Metrics` as that work defines it.
- **Engine knob coverage** (individual `engine:` fields): owned per engine release by the engine's rules packs.
- **Autoscaling and the other `--policy-config` settings on `Deployment`.** BLIS's autoscaler, node pools, instance lifecycle, priority and preemption settings are read from a separate `--policy-config` YAML ([`sim/bundle.go#L20`](https://github.com/inference-sim/inference-sim/blob/1813579275e3f782ecc1a83ef508017935121235/sim/bundle.go#L20)), outside the `Scenario` and `Deployment`. Folding them into the deployment document is #1602's scope; until then they are inputs a `Result` records under `input.policy` (verbatim) so that the round-trip in section C still holds. SLO targets stay on the workload (`goodput_slo_targets`).
- **Offload description.** #1910 unifies `Deployment.offload` and `--kv-offload-config`; once it lands, the offload configuration is part of `input.deployment` like everything else.
- **Removing CLI flags.** #1602.

## Delivery

| Step | Repo | Issue | Depends on | State |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. `measurement` vocabulary: `Clock: simulated` | blis-schemas | #108 | - | done (PR #15) |
| 2. `spec/result` (`Result`), validator, loader, `Bundle.Result`, example document | blis-schemas | #4 | 1 | done (PR #15) |
| 3. blis-schemas release carrying 1-2 | blis-schemas | - | 2 | done (`v0.9.0`) |
| 4. `run` / `replay` emit the `Result` (JSON default, `--format yaml`), `--output`, `--view summary`; deprecate `--metrics-path` / `--results-path`; INV-6 and INV-13 restated over the `Result` | inference-sim | inference-sim/inference-sim#1871 | 3 | done (PR inference-sim/inference-sim#2058) |
| 4a. Record output-only flags that change the document; closed-loop follow-ups field | inference-sim | inference-sim/inference-sim#2062 | 4 | open |
| 4b. `engine` section from `engine.Engine.Metrics`; series by reference | inference-sim (+ blis-schemas `engine`, blis-vllm) | inference-sim/inference-sim#2070 | 4 | open |
| 5. `--from-result`, `rerun_of` / `revision_changes`; round-trip tests | inference-sim | inference-sim/inference-sim#2054 | 4 | open |
| 6. Consumers read the `Result` | accuracy-dashboard, blis-config-search | inference-sim/accuracy-dashboard#44, inference-sim/blis-config-search#20 | 4 | config-search done; dashboard open |
| 7. Remove `--metrics-path` / `--results-path` | inference-sim | inference-sim/inference-sim#2071 | 6 | open |

Step 4 shipped before the engine reported through `engine.Engine.Metrics`, so inference-sim fills `Result.engine` from the series it emits itself; step 4b moves it to the engine's own report. The sweep types (`spec/sweep`) are a separate blis-schemas addition that consumes the `Result`; they do not block it.

## Decisions

- **Name:** `Result` (`kind: Result`, package `spec/result`).
- **Encoding:** JSON by default; YAML with `--format yaml`. Both carry the same document.
- **Run controls:** recorded in `Result.input.run`; they stay CLI flags, and sweeps are `SweepSpec`'s job, so there is no standalone run-controls document.
- **Re-running on a newer BLIS:** allowed; the new `Result` records `rerun_of` and `revision_changes`.

# KF-RD-GENAI-STACK-2026-001

## Purpose

milestone.title: Downstream failure diagnosability and containment
milestone.description:
Downstream failure diagnosability, and containment of the failures we cannot prevent.

Measured on production, 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-04: 96 downstream failures were recorded and every one of them stored a null downstream duration, so no query could tell an AI Service failure apart from gateway time. On 2026-10-04 the AI Speaking service returned HTTP 500 to 55 consecutive calls on one operation inside one hour; the operator log recorded the status and the duration, and nothing the provider said about why. Twelve contract violations recorded on 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-02 are now undiagnosable, because the container that served them was replaced and the log went with it.

Done means two things. A customer-reported failure can be explained from durable records alone: the log outlives the container, a 4xx or 5xx entry carries the provider's own code and a sanitized message, and every failure record carries the measured downstream duration. And a failing AI Service stops taking the traffic that fails with it, which is #199 and not a diagnosability change.

- #234 keeps the operator log diagnosable after its container is replaced
- #235 carries the provider's own code and a sanitized message on 4xx and 5xx
- #236 records the downstream duration on the failure path
- #199 adds a per-operation circuit breaker on the dispatch path, which acts on a downstream failure rather than explaining one

items.body:
## Parent

#268

## What to build

The downstream HTTP pool's real concurrency matches what the gateway admits, so a request never waits in a hidden client-side queue while its deadline runs down.

The pool allows 10 connections per origin. Under HTTP/1.1, its current configuration allows at most 10 requests to reach an origin at once, so excess admitted work waits inside the client while its deadline runs down. Under HTTP/2, connections multiplex streams: a 10-socket setting is not a 10-request ceiling and does not by itself establish a safe provider capacity. An organization may hold 20 concurrent requests by default, and several organizations share one origin. Align admission with the actual per-origin request/stream budget for the negotiated protocol, rather than assuming multiplexing removes the capacity problem.

Furthermore, `inFlightByOrigin` in `src/modules/gateway/infrastructure/dispatch/downstream-http.client.ts` enforces a flat `MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_PER_ORIGIN = 10` bulkhead across all operations sharing a downstream origin. On origins hosting both heavy 60s grading dispatches and lightweight status reads (`speaking.v2.response-get` ~50ms), concurrent grading uploads saturate the origin bulkhead and reject fast score reads with immediate 503 `ai_service:bulkhead_exhausted`.

## Triage questions

- Do the production AI Writing and AI Speaking origins negotiate h2? Check the ALPN result.
- What concurrency can each AI Service actually serve? Raising the client ceiling past that moves the queue to the provider.

## Local HTTP/2 capacity evidence (2026-10-25)

At `3d3d29cf8a2999d57dbdef1ce231fde846320876`, a localhost TLS HTTP/2 server held response bodies open while the actual client used its own [managed pool configuration](https://github.com/AiHub-Ecosystem/aihub-be/blob/3d3d29cf8a2999d57dbdef1ce231fde846320876/src/modules/gateway/infrastructure/downstream-http.client.ts#L269), not a replacement dispatcher. After warming the connection, all 11 concurrent requests reached the server and remained active over one HTTP/2 session before any was released, despite `connections: 10`. All completed after release. This confirms that the configured socket count is not an aggregate HTTP/2 request ceiling. It does not measure provider throughput or justify raising any capacity.

The harness used Windows Node 24.21.0 and installed Undici 8.12.2. The earlier production ALPN evidence remains a historical probe; this audit did not re-probe production protocols or idle timeouts. HTTP/1.1 queue cancellation remains #834, body byte limits remain #377, and protocol-specific body failures are #1187.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Establish Writing origin admission across the four Uvicorn workers and every caller sharing port 8001, including Production, Sandbox and direct service routes. Bound active provider work and queued work separately, choose an explicit short admission wait/refusal contract, and recheck work eligibility before each provider send. Kernel backlog, nginx connection limits, Gunicorn worker count and per-client HTTPX pool size are not interchangeable model-capacity budgets. Coordinate tenant/environment shares with #398 and cancellation with #1199.
- [ ] Establish the Speaking capacity bound across the full parallel provider pipeline, not just active SpeechAce calls. Define/verify STT/LLM shared admission, slot ownership beyond lease expiry, fixed-window boundary bursts, and startup Redis failure behavior. A phase timeout or configured concurrency value alone is not a sustainable-throughput or hard global-capacity proof; coordinate cleanup with #1198.
- [ ] Differentiate connection pool and inFlight bulkhead limits between long-running multipart grading requests (20s-60s) and fast result queries (e.g. `speaking.v2.response-get` ~50ms) sharing the same downstream origin, so that active uploads do not exhaust the origin bulkhead and starve fast status reads.
- [x] The negotiated protocol for each production origin is recorded in this issue
- [ ] The queued-request metric from the observability slice shows whether requests ever wait in the pool under normal traffic
- [ ] If they do: the connection ceiling, or an explicit gateway-side ceiling, is set from the provider's stated capacity, and the choice is written next to the pool configuration
- [ ] The pool's idle keep-alive is shorter than each provider origin's own idle timeout, and the two values are recorded next to the pool configuration. The pool keeps an idle socket for up to 300 s when the origin sends no `Keep-Alive: timeout=` hint. If the origin (or a proxy in front of it) closes idle connections sooner, a grading sent on a socket the server is closing at that moment fails mid-request. undici does not replay a `POST`, so the request ends as a downstream failure with an unknown outcome. A test or a recorded probe shows each production origin's idle timeout. (Added 2026-10-20 from the API and protocol audit.)
- [ ] The capacity choice distinguishes socket count from active HTTP/2 streams and states the aggregate per-origin request budget for every supported protocol, including its process/replica scope. Peer-advertised stream capacity is not substituted for the provider owner's measured model-serving capacity.
- [ ] Local HTTP/1.1 and TLS HTTP/2 regressions hold requests open and verify the chosen admission/queue behavior using the real managed pool. A protocol negotiation change cannot silently multiply admitted downstream work or invalidate the HTTP/1.1 baseline without being recorded; coordinate with #398/#327.
- [x] `pnpm verify` passes

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately. #269, which blocked this issue, is closed.
